replies.text:
Checks (step 2 list):
- Automated abuse of reachable endpoints: present — "There is no rate limiting yet." Covered by listed threats 3, 4, 5.
- Staff/admin/moderator screens showing user-supplied content: design says nothing of the kind — not applicable.
- Delete/moderate/refund/approve/role-change with no record: no such action in design; accountability of key use already covered by listed threat 6.
- Personal/account data pages that browsers, shared proxies or CDNs could store: present — a public GET-style API returning "all of the partner's orders and customer email addresses" with the credential "in the query string"; listed threat 2 covers the key leaking via proxies/logs, but not the order/email response itself being stored and served from shared caches — not covered.
- Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, CSV exports, emails or headers: design states no such sink — not applicable.
- Single-reviewer threats: #1 duplicates listed 5; #3 and #4 depend on unstated implementation detail of how partner/order ids are derived — excluded; #2 (one key grants everything, no scoping) is stated verbatim in the design and no listed threat addresses least privilege — not covered.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-01",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Public REST API", "API key auth", "Orders endpoint", "Partner integrations"],
    "dataStores": ["orders"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["internet to public API", "partner org to our API"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii", "secrets"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "One unscoped key grants all orders and customer emails, no least privilege",
      "scenario": "A partner integration that only needs order status is issued the same single key that grants access to all of that partner's orders and every customer email address on them. No scopes or read-level split is described. Compromise of a minor partner tool, a developer laptop, or a curious partner employee therefore immediately yields the full personal-data set rather than the narrow slice the integration needed, and we cannot issue a status-only credential to reduce exposure.",
      "component": "Public REST API key authorisation",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "insider", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [ { "quote": "Keys never expire and grant access to all of the partner’s orders and customer email addresses." } ],
      "asvs": ["V8.3.4"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-272"],
      "plainLanguage": "Every partner key unlocks everything, so even a small integration carries a credential that can read all customer emails.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Scope partner API keys to the minimum data needed",
        "given": "a partner integration that only needs order status",
        "when": "an API key is issued and used against the orders endpoint",
        "then": "the key carries explicit scopes and customer email addresses are only returned to keys granted a personal-data scope, with the scope recorded at issuance"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Order and customer-email responses stored by browsers, shared proxies or CDNs",
      "scenario": "Because the credential is in the URL, the orders request looks like a plain cacheable GET to intermediaries. A shared corporate proxy, CDN or browser cache can store the response body containing a partner's orders and customer email addresses and later serve or expose it to someone who never held the key, for example another user of the same proxy or anyone reading the cache store. The harm here is customer personal data, not just the key.",
      "component": "Public REST API orders responses",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "medium", "reach": "many", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [ { "quote": "Partners call our public REST API with an API key in the query string." } ],
      "asvs": ["V8.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-525"],
      "plainLanguage": "Customer order and email responses could be saved by caches or proxies and seen by people who never had the API key.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Mark personal-data API responses non-cacheable",
        "given": "an API response containing orders and customer email addresses",
        "when": "the response is returned to a partner",
        "then": "it is sent with no-store cache directives and is not cached by any CDN or shared proxy in the request path"
      }
    }
  ]
}
